reviews.plausible_gain_reasoning: The 48.5% is a fouling-detachment-stress reduction, not a friction change; clean-hull compliant-wall drag reduction at ship Reynolds numbers is unproven and the streamwise ribs even stiffen the wall in the streamwise direction, so a friction gain of ~0-0.5% is the realistic range.
key_assumption_issues: Metric is fouling detachment stress while the request's primary benefit is frictional drag.
The claimed anisotropy (streamwise compliant, spanwise stiff) is contradicted by the model itself: streamwise ribs clamp streamwise shear displacement too.
Ribs are modelled as full height and rigid, while the concept has 60% height ribs; compliance and gain are therefore uncertain by a factor ~1.5-2.
Shear compliance used as proxy for normal pull-off compliance.
killer_risks: Soft 0.1 MPa top still gouged by fenders; ribs only limit crack length, not damage initiation.
Rib edges telegraph through the soft top under point loads and create roughness that adds drag.
2 mm soft build plus rib structure costs several times a standard foul-release system.
Slime (diatom) fouling at low speeds not addressed.

reviews.plausible_gain_reasoning: The concept does not act on the flow at all; its friction benefit versus a clean foul-release coating is zero, and the 84% interfacial stress reduction concerns stresses that are already ~100x below adhesion strength.
key_assumption_issues: Metric (peak shear-lag stress from hull strain) addresses a failure mode that does not govern foul-release service life.
Baseline tie-coat stiffness (20 MPa, 0.1 mm) chosen by the auditor; real tie-coats vary widely, so the 84% depends on that choice.
Shear-lag ignores peel stresses, which dominate real edge debonding.
killer_risks: No drag benefit at all, the request's main goal.
Real delamination is driven by impact, abrasion, osmosis and surface preparation, which the gradient barely affects.
A thick graded layer adds material, drying time and QA effort in the dock.
